questions.q: Why does Mrs Lithebe, unlike most people, not let rooms to strangers?
choices: Her late husband, a builder, built her a fine big house and she 'has money enough'; she keeps rooms only for the priest and for Gertrude and the child
questions.explain: She thinks it 'good to have prayers in the house.'

questions.q: What kindness does Kumalo ask of Mrs Lithebe in this chapter?
choices: To take in the girl who is with child by Absalom, to get her away from Pimville
questions.explain: Mrs Lithebe agrees; the girl can sleep on the floor of the room where they eat — 'better... than to...'.

questions.q: Where must Kumalo now get money from, his own being nearly gone?
choices: From the Post Office Book — the ten pounds saved for his wife's stove
questions.explain: His wife must wait longer for her stove, and he for his new black clothes and collars.

questions.q: What does Mrs Lithebe warn the girl about, in the kitchen?
choices: Her 'careless laughter' — 'This old man has been hurt greatly... he shall not be hurt any more, not in my house'
questions.explain: The girl answers each warning with 'I understand you completely.'

questions.q: How does the girl behave in Mrs Lithebe's house, compared with Gertrude?
choices: She is 'openly glad to be in this house', calls Mrs Lithebe 'mother', and is obedient and quick to learn
questions.explain: She had never before lived in such a house; she can speak Sesuto 'after a broken fashion.'

choices: The tall, grave lawyer who will take Absalom's case
questions.explain: He looks 'like a man used to great matters, much greater than the case of a black boy who has killed a man.'

questions.q: On what terms does Mr Carmichael take the case?
choices: For a large fee paid by John
'Pro deo' — for God, meaning for nothing, or at least very little
For a share of any damages
questions.explain: Father Vincent explains the Latin phrase to Kumalo, who has not heard it before.

questions.q: What did the other two accused do when the police brought them face to face with Absalom?
choices: They cursed him and said 'How can he lie so about us?'
questions.explain: Their defence will be that they were never there at all.

questions.q: Why does Carmichael say he cannot defend Matthew Kumalo and Johannes Pafuri?
choices: Their defence — that they were not present — directly contradicts Absalom's truthful account, which Carmichael believes
questions.explain: He inclines to the opinion that Absalom has no motive to implicate them falsely.

questions.q: How does Father Vincent describe the lawyer to Kumalo?
choices: 'One of the greatest lawyers in South Africa and one of the greatest friends of your people'
'A man who takes any case for money'
questions.explain: 'You may thank God that we have got this man.'
